steps.calloutText: Illustrative 80,000-loan portfolio with real facility emissions from Climate TRACE and EDGAR underneath.
steps.narration: Welcome. What you are looking at is the financed-emissions dashboard for Laxmi Sunrise Bank. The loan book on this tab is an illustrative 80,000-loan portfolio used to walk through the platform. The numbers underneath every record are real, drawn from Climate TRACE satellite verification and EDGAR national inventories through Jana Earth Data. Over the next three and a half minutes I will walk you through how a bank uses this platform to meet all three of Nepal Rastra Bank's environmental regulations through a single data platform.

steps.calloutText: ESRM screens new loans · Taxonomy classifies the book · NFRS produces annual disclosures.
steps.narration: The tabs across the top map directly onto NRB's regulatory stack. ESRM from the 2018 directive is the credit decision layer. every new commercial loan gets screened for environmental risk before approval. Taxonomy from October 2024 classifies the entire book as green, amber, or red. And NFRS, coming in 2026 and 2027, requires public disclosure of financed emissions under the PCAF methodology. Most banks are stuck on all three because they don't have facility-level emissions data. Jana provides that data layer.

steps.calloutTitle: Small by count. Large by value. All the regulatory risk.
steps.calloutText: About 1,000 commercial exposures in this illustrative book have facility-tier data, behind roughly 120 unique borrowers spanning cement, hydropower, industry, and logistics.
steps.narration: Here is the picture that matters for any bank. In this illustrative 80,000-loan book, roughly 10,000 loans are non-retail business exposures that fall under NRB regulation. Of those 10,000 in-scope loans, roughly 1,000 are large commercial and corporate exposures where facility-level emissions data attaches. Behind those 1,000 loans sit roughly 120 unique borrowers with verified satellite emissions, spanning cement, hydropower, hotels, logistics, waste utilities, and large industrial. By count that is a small slice. By outstanding value it is the slice that carries almost all of the environmental risk a regulator examines. Every commercial bank in Nepal has a version of this picture. The mix varies by institution.

steps.calloutTitle: Tier 1 — screen new loans before approval
steps.calloutText: Every commercial loan application gets an environmental risk assessment using real facility data, not borrower self-reporting.
steps.narration: Let's start with a new credit application. This is what a compliance officer at Laxmi sees when a commercial loan comes across their desk. Real applications, real borrowers. Each one needs an environmental risk assessment in the loan file before the credit committee approves it. The bank then reports the aggregated results to Nepal Rastra Bank every quarter. Without Jana, that assessment is a manual research project per borrower. With Jana, it is a single API call.

steps.calloutText: Real Climate TRACE 2024 emissions: roughly 922,000 tonnes CO₂e. About 4.9% of Nepal's national CO₂.
steps.narration: Let's drill into one borrower. Hongshi-Shivam Cement, a Chinese-Nepali joint venture and the country's largest cement plant. The numbers you see here are not estimates. The facility coordinates come from the Global Cement Tracker. The 922,000 tonnes of CO₂ figure comes from Climate TRACE satellite verification for 2024. The national-share metric, about 4.9 percent, comes from EDGAR's Nepal CO₂ inventory. A single facility, attributable to a single loan, contributing nearly five percent of an entire country's carbon emissions. That is the kind of exposure a credit committee needs to see before they approve a large working capital line.

steps.calloutText: Coordinates match the GCCT registry. Verified by Climate TRACE assets. Auditable down to the dot.
steps.narration: This is the facility on a map. Coordinates from the Global Cement and Concrete Tracker, emissions from Climate TRACE's satellite data product, ownership from the Global Energy Monitor entity registry. Every number on this screen is sourced, citable, and reproducible. When NRB examines this loan three years from now, Laxmi can show exactly where the data came from.

steps.calloutText: PCAF-compliant Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions, ready for the annual report.
steps.narration: Fast-forward to the end of the year. Laxmi needs to file its annual sustainability report under NFRS. Nepal's IFRS S2-aligned disclosure framework. This is the dashboard the CFO and CRO see. Total financed emissions across the book, with the most recent fully-reported year, and a multi-year trend. The number on the page is what goes into the annual report, with full PCAF methodology attribution underneath.

steps.calloutTitle: PCAF data quality — the technical moat
steps.calloutText: Without Jana: Score 5 across the board. With Jana: Score 2 on the slice that matters.
steps.narration: And here is the technical differentiator. PCAF requires every bank to disclose a data quality score from 1 to 5, with 1 being best. Without facility-level data, a bank defaults to Score 5. revenue-based estimates using national averages. With Jana, the highest-emission slice of the portfolio moves to Score 2. satellite-verified facility data plus public financial filings. NRB examiners and IFRS S2 auditors both look at this score. Jana moves the needle on the loans that matter.
